newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end higher as foreign buyers return.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end higher as foreign buyers return.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed higher on Friday for the second straight session amid renewed foreign interest piqued by signs of waning labor strife, traders said.

The market's leading 19-share .IBC index rose 1.85 percent to close at 6,642.05 points, as nearly 40 million shares worth 5.3 billion bolivars ($11.2 million) changed hands, according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"Foreign investors are back on the good news of the past few days," said Interacciones broker Freddy Zambrano, who saw the trend extending into next week.
After almost two months of strikes, the government on Wednesday offered public sector workers a 35 percent pay rise plus a 50 percent increase in monthly bonuses.
The proposal has been provisionally accepted by the country's largest union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers, but it must still pass muster with others.
"Investor interest has certainly picked up ... with strong offers for Electricidad de Caracas," said Credit Lyonnais broker Peter Ryan in New York.
Among the stocks that were traded, 27 rose, eight fell and 11 were unchanged.
